item.title: Patrick Clancy Threatens Legal Action Over False Murder Claims
item.description: Patrick Clancy’s lawyers warned of legal action over baseless claims linking him to his three children’s deaths. His ex-wife Lindsay’s murder trial ended in a September 2026 mistrial, with jurors divided over her criminal responsibility.

item.title: Sarah Grace Patrick’s TikTok Tributes Before Murder Charges
item.description: Sarah Grace Patrick posted TikTok tributes to her mother and stepfather, Kristin and James Brock, after their deaths in Georgia. Creators say she also requested coverage of the killings before her July 2025 arrest. She has pleaded not guilty to murder charges, with trial scheduled for February 2027.

item.title: The Well Behind The Liu Mansion’s Ghost Legend
item.description: Built in 1929, Taiwan’s Liu family mansion became known as the Minxiong Ghost House. Its best-known legend concerns a maid said to have died in its well. Accounts of the family’s departure point to work and schooling elsewhere; the haunting stories remain unverified.

item.title: A Brain Scan Emerged After Her Jury Deadlocked
item.description: Dena Schlosser killed her infant daughter, Margaret, in Plano, Texas, in 2004. After a mistrial, a psychiatrist testified that a brain tumor might explain her hallucinations. In 2006, a judge found her not guilty by reason of insanity and ordered psychiatric hospitalization.

item.title: Her Killer Entered Prison. Her Cousin Was Already There
item.description: Anthony Stockelman pleaded guilty to killing 10-year-old Katie Collman in Indiana and received life without parole. In 2006, her cousin Jared Harris tattooed “Katie’s Revenge” on Stockelman’s forehead inside prison, prompting a battery charge against Harris.

item.title: The Sunken Car Behind Lake Lanier’s Ghost Story
item.description: Susie Roberts and Delia Parker Young disappeared into Georgia’s Lake Lanier after a 1958 car crash. Workers recovered Roberts’ car and remains in 1990. Their deaths became linked to the “Lady of the Lake” legend, but reported ghost sightings remain unverified.
